runware.label: Runware
runware.source: the service's API documentation and parameter schemas

auth.note: The key is read from the environment or a local credential store at run time; it is never written into a record, a spec, or a run file.

envelope.request: A JSON array of task objects. Each task carries taskType and a client-generated taskUUID, and the task's own parameters at the top level of the object.
envelope.response: An object with data (one entry per finished task, carrying the taskUUID) or errors (one entry per refused task with code, message, parameter, documentation, and taskUUID). A submission can be refused per task while the request itself succeeds.

imageInference.input: model, positivePrompt, negativePrompt, width, height, steps, CFGScale, scheduler, seed, and optionally seedImage (an uploaded image id) with strength

videoInference.input: model, positivePrompt, duration, width and height (or a resolution preset), and the input mode's media keys (frameImages, referenceImages) as uploaded image ids; deliveryMethod async

imageUpload.purpose: register a local image for use as a seed image, frame image, or reference
imageUpload.input: image as a data URI (base64) with its MIME type
imageUpload.note: Uploads can be cached locally by content hash; the same bytes need not be uploaded twice.

getResponse.returns: the task's data entry when finished, with videoURL or imageURL; a status of processing otherwise

mediaStorage.purpose: store media of any kind (video, audio, image) for later use as a reference video or audio
mediaStorage.input: operation upload with media as a data URI; operation delete with the media id
mediaStorage.note: imageUpload is the image-only path; a video sent through it is not an upload route. The task type list the service returns on an invalid taskType is the authoritative inventory of operations.

imageUpscale.purpose: enlarge one image with an upscaler model
imageUpscale.input: model, inputs.image (an uploaded image id, URL, or data URI), upscaleFactor, and the model's settings; outputType, outputFormat, and outputQuality as for imageInference

video.poll: getResponse by taskUUID at an interval of about ten seconds; a five-second clip returns in two to three minutes
video.terminal: videoURL present in the data entry
video.note: A task refused at submission (an error entry in the submission response) answers processing when polled afterwards and never finishes. Read the submission response before polling.

errors.shape: errors[] entries with code, message, parameter, and where the service offers it a documentation URL and the taskUUID

observed_codes.invalidVideoDurationInteger: duration outside the model's integer band; the band itself is a fact of the model's offering, not of the service
observed_codes.invalidTaskType: an unknown taskType; the response lists every supported task type
observed_codes.unsupportedIpAdapterModel: the adapter's architecture does not match the checkpoint's registered architecture string; the response names both

batch.value: several tasks in one request are accepted; this suite's projects send one task per request

adapter_compatibility.value: Adapter compatibility (IP-Adapter, ControlNet, LoRA) is checked against the architecture string the checkpoint was registered with, not against its weights. An uploaded checkpoint registered under a fine-tune family name can be refused adapters that the same weights accept when registered as the base family. The allowed architecture strings for a checkpoint upload are exactlyai_image, flux1d, flux1s, fluxkontextdev, illustrious, noobai, pony, sd1x, sdxl, sdxllightning, sdxlturbo, z_image, z_image_turbo; the documentation does not say what the string changes at inference. One lineage rendered identically under noobai, sdxl, and illustrious registrations.
